question: Your extraction pipeline processes invoices through the synchronous Claude API. For each invoice, Claude calls a lookup_vendor tool, your code runs the database lookup and returns the result, and Claude then finishes the JSON extraction. A teammate proposes moving the nightly run of 40,000 invoices to the Message Batches API to cut costs. Which limitation of the batch API must the redesign account for?

options.text: The Message Batches API guarantees completion within one hour, so the nightly run must be split into several smaller hourly batches.
options.reason: The guide says the batch API has up to a 24-hour processing window and no guaranteed latency SLA, so there is no one-hour guarantee.

options.text: Batch results can arrive in any order, and the API offers no way to match each response to its originating invoice request.
options.reason: The guide names custom_id fields as the way to correlate batch request and response pairs, so matching is supported.

options.text: A batch request cannot pause for your code to run the vendor lookup and return its result to Claude mid-request.
options.reason: The guide states that the batch API does not support multi-turn tool calling within a single request, so tools cannot be executed mid-request with results returned.

options.text: The Message Batches API suits only blocking workflows, so a nightly run that no one waits on should stay on the synchronous API.
options.reason: The guide says batch processing fits non-blocking, latency-tolerant workloads such as overnight jobs and is inappropriate for blocking workflows, the reverse of this claim.
